Question 3

Consider the following boundary value problem (BVP).

y″−4y=0,2y(0)−y′(0)=2y(1)−y′(1)=0,0≤x≤1

Let y1(x) and y2(x) be the fundamental solutions, and suppose we define the matrix A as

A=[2y1(0)−y1′(0)2y2(0)−y2′(0)2y1(1)−y1′(1)2y2(1)−y2′(1)].

Fill in the correct options in the reasoning below.

The boundary value problem has a unique solution if and only if
 
det(A)=0
det(A)≠0
.

The fundamental solutions to this BVP are
 
y1(x)=e2x and y2(x)=e−2x
y1(x)=e4x and y2(x)=e−x
y1(x)=cos⁡(2x) and y2(x)=sin⁡(2x)
y1(x)=e−2x and y2(x)=xe−2x
.

For this BVP, we have det(A)=
 
16e2
4(e2−e−2)
−16
0
−4(e2+e−2)
.

Therefore, this BVP
 
has infinitely many solutions
has no solution
has the unique solution y≡0
.
